checked_steps: Rest in the shade.
If you have a wide-brimmed hat, wear it to shield your face and neck from the sun.
Avoid hard activity during the hottest part of the day if you can.
Drink plenty of water, even if you don't feel thirsty.
The temperature inside a parked vehicle can rapidly rise to a dangerous level for children, pets and even adults.
Don't ration your drinking water unless authorities tell you to. Drink what you need today and try to find more for tomorrow.
Streams, rivers and other moving water can be sources of water.
Water from outdoor sources must be treated to kill germs before you drink it.
If the water might have fuel or chemicals in it, don't drink it. Boiling won't make it safe.
If the water is cloudy, first filter it through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter.
Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute. Above 6,500 feet, boil it for 3 minutes.
Do not drink seawater. Drinking seawater can be deadly to humans.
Melt snow before drinking it. Eating unmelted snow will lower your body temperature.
Stop. Take a moment to calmly look at your situation.
If you have a map, compass or GPS, or can see landmarks, use them to try to work out where you are.
If it's safe, retrace your steps to get back to the route you planned.
If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are.
Changing location will make it hard for searchers to find you. Move only if there is an immediate threat to life.
